# Common JVM options for every packaged desktop target. One option per line.
# Keep the heap bounded: QPlayer's measured post-GC live set is well below this,
# while the JDK default reserved 25% of host RAM (about 4 GiB on a 16 GiB PC).
-XX:+UseG1GC
-Xms32m
-Xmx768m
-Xss512k

# QML generates many small classes and call sites, but measured usage is about
# 7 MiB of class space and 30 MiB of code. These retain generous headroom while
# avoiding the JDK defaults of 1 GiB and 240 MiB respectively.
-XX:CompressedClassSpaceSize=128m
-XX:ReservedCodeCacheSize=128m

# Avoid sizing GC/JIT worker pools from a high core-count desktop. Two workers
# preserve responsive incremental collection without Serial GC's frame-length
# stop-the-world pauses.
-XX:CICompilerCount=2
-XX:ParallelGCThreads=2
-XX:ConcGCThreads=1
-XX:G1ConcRefinementThreads=2

# The defaults retain 40-70% free heap after collection. QPlayer's QML compile
# has a short allocation spike, so those ratios otherwise keep hundreds of MiB
# committed after the first frame even though the live set is much smaller.
-XX:MinHeapFreeRatio=10
-XX:MaxHeapFreeRatio=20

# Return unused regions after long idle/background periods instead of retaining
# the high-water mark for the rest of a music session.
-XX:G1PeriodicGCInterval=300000
